'''Sir George Ernest Francis Wood''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|KBE|ISO|size=85%}} (13 July 1900 – 18 December 1978) was a New Zealand economist and statistician. He served as government statistician in Palestine from 1938 to 1945, New Zealand [[Statistics NZ#History|government statistician]] from 1946 to 1958, and chair of the [[Consumer NZ|Consumer Council]] from 1959 to 1975. Wood chaired the [[United Nations Statistical Commission]] from 1958 to 1960, and was a director of the [[Reserve Bank of New Zealand|Reserve Bank]] between 1959 and 1963.

==Early life and family==
Born in [[Greymouth]] on 13 July 1900, Wood was the son of George Francis and Margaret Wood.<ref name="Whos who">{{cite book |editor-last=Traue |editor-first=J. E. |editor-link=Jim Traue |title=Who's Who in New Zealand |edition=11th |year=1978 |publisher=Reed |location=Wellington |isbn=0-589-01113-8 |page=292}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bdmhistoricalrecords.dia.govt.nz/search/search?path=%2FqueryEntry.m%3Ftype%3Dbirths |title=Birth search: registration number 1900/13198 |website=Births, deaths & marriages online |publisher=Department of Internal Affairs |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> He was educated at [[Greymouth District High School]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/GEST19160203.2.53 |title=Greymouth District High School |date=3 February 1916 |work=Greymouth Evening Star |page=7 |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> and went on to study economics at [[Victoria University of Wellington|Victoria University College]], graduating [[Master of Arts]] with second-class honours in 1924.<ref name="Whos who"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university25.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: Wi–Z |website=Shadows of Time |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref>

On 3 September 1928, Wood married Eileen Alice Oudaille,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bdmhistoricalrecords.dia.govt.nz/search/search?path=%2FqueryEntry.m%3Ftype%3Dmarriages |title=Marriage search: registration number 1928/3446 |website=Births, deaths & marriages online |publisher=Department of Internal Affairs |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> and the couple went on to have two children.<ref name="Whos who"/>

==Career==
Wood began his public service career in March 1918, working in the Police Department.<ref name="AG 1946">{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/AG19460812.2.11 |title=Personal |date=12 August 1946 |work=Ashburton Guardian |volume=66 |issue=257 |page=2 |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> He moved to the [[Statistics New Zealand|Office of Census and Statistics]] (later the Department of Statistics and now Statistics New Zealand), in 1921,<ref name="Press obituary">{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19781221.2.104 |title=Former statistics chief dead |date=21 December 1978 |work=[[The Press]] |page=11 |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> and rose to become chief compiler in 1937.<ref name="AG 1946"/> Between 1938 and 1945, he was seconded to the [[British Colonial Service]] and was the government statistician in [[Mandatory Palestine|Palestine]],<ref name="Whos who"/><ref name="AG 1946"/> in recognition of which service he was appointed an [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] in the [[1946 New Year Honours]].<ref>{{London Gazette |date=28 December 1945 |issue=37407 |page=63}}</ref>

After his return to New Zealand, Wood served as acting government statistician for a few months, before taking up the substantive role of government statistician on 9 August 1946.<ref name="AG 1946"/> He remained in that position until his retirement at the end of January 1958.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19580111.2.67 |title=Personal items |date=11 January 1958 |work=[[The Press]] |volume=97 |issue=28482 |page=10 |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> During his tenure, the Statistics Department began producing [[balance of payments]] data again in 1950 after a 22-year hiatus, and increased the level of detail in the information. He instigated the [[consumer price index]] (CPI) in New Zealand, and ensured that the figures were released in a timely fashion, generally within 10 days of the end of the period under review. Wood expanded the department's research capacity, and it began population forecasting, rather than just producing historical data, and drawing up actuarial [[life table]]s, which also included data relating to [[Māori people|Māori]] for the first time.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://www.stats.org.nz/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/A-History-of-Statistics-in-New-Zealand-1.pdf |chapter=Sir George Ernest Francis Wood (1900–1978), Government Statistician (1946–1958) |first=Kristeene |last=Parkes |title=A History of Statistics in New Zealand |year=1999 |editor-last=Roberts |editor-first=H. S. |publisher=New Zealand Statistical Association |location=Wellington |isbn=0-9597632-7-9 |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> In 1953, Wood received the [[Queen Elizabeth II Coronation Medal]],<ref>{{cite book |last1=Taylor |first1=Alister |last2=Coddington |first2=Deborah |author-link1=Alister Taylor |author-link2=Deborah Coddington |title=Honoured by the Queen – New Zealand |year=1994 |publisher=New Zealand Who's Who Aotearoa |location=Auckland |isbn=0-908578-34-2 |page=423}}</ref> and in the [[1956 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|1956 Queen's Birthday Honours]], he was appointed a [[Companion of the Imperial Service Order]].<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=40789 |date=31 May 1956 |page=3145 |supp=3}}</ref>

After his retirement as government statistician, Wood was elected chair of the 10th session of the United Nations Statistical Commission, from 1958 to 1960. The New Zealand prime minister at the time, [[Walter Nash]], paid tribute to Wood, saying: "I am sure that he will give just as valuable service to the world—through United Nations—as he has given New Zealand".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19580430.2.50 |title=U.N. Statistical Commission |date=30 April 1958 |work=[[The Press]] |volume=97 |issue=28573 |page=7 |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref>

Wood served as a director of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand from 1958 to 1963.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19750614.2.15 |title=New knights noted for public service |date=14 June 1975 |work=[[The Press]] |volume=115 |issue=33869 |page=1 |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref>

In July 1959, Wood was appointed inaugural chair of the Consumer Council (later called the Consumers' Institute, and now known as Consumer NZ) by the Minister of Industries and Commerce, [[Phil Holloway]], who said that the council was "fortunate in having the services of a man of the calibre and experience of Mr Wood who had made a special study of prices and the distribution of national income", and that "he could think of no-one better qualified to guide the council in its work".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19590714.2.10 |title=National Consumer Council citizen members chosen |date=14 July 1959 |work=[[The Press]] |volume=98 |issue=28946 |page=3 |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> He retired from the role of chair on 25 June 1975. The then-prime minister, [[Bill Rowling]], said that Wood had played a vital part in the development of the organisation. The leader of the opposition, [[Robert Muldoon]], noted that Wood's integrity had never been questioned.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19750628.2.155 |title='Watchdog' role |date=28 June 1975 |work=[[The Press]] |volume=115 |issue=33881 |page=17 |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> During Wood's 16 years as chair, the membership of the Consumers' Institute had gone from 1772 in the first year to 129,000, which Wood said was testament to "the impartial and incorruptible approach of the council to its work".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19750507.2.120 |title=Chairman's farewell visit |date=7 May 1975 |work=[[The Press]] |issue=33836 |page=20 |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> Wood was intimately involved in the establishment of a complaints advisory service in 1973, which quickly grew to hear 12,648 complaints the following year and obtained redress in 98.8 per cent of cases deemed to warrant it.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19750627.2.154 |title=Sir George Wood (75) looks to the future |date=27 June 1975 |work=[[The Press]] |volume=115 |issue=33880 |page=17 |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref>

In the [[1975 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|1975 Queen's Birthday Honours]], Wood was promoted to [[Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire]], for public services, especially as chairman of the Consumer Council since 1959.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=46595 |date=14 June 1975 |page=7405 |supp=3}}</ref>

==Later life and death==
The Woods moved to [[Whangārei]] around 1970.<ref>{{cite book |title=1969 Wellington Central electoral district: main roll of persons entitled to vote for Members of Parliament of New Zealand |date=30 July 1969 |page=191}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=1972 Whangarei electoral district: main roll of persons entitled to vote for Members of Parliament of New Zealand |date=26 July 1972 |page=355}}</ref> Wood died there on 18 December 1978, and was buried at Maunu Cemetery.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://old.wdc.govt.nz/SearchCentre/Pages/CemeteryBurialDetails.aspx?CMID=4210&CMType=burial |title=Cemetery record details |publisher=Whangarei District Council |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> [[Jack Lewin]], government statistician from 1969 to 1973, paid tribute, saying that Wood was "small in inches but big in stature".<ref name="Press obituary"/> He went on to say:<blockquote>Greater than his statistical ability and more remarkable were his unsubduable courage and his unerring instinct for fairness and decency.<ref name="Press obituary"/></blockquote>

Eileen, Lady Wood, died in 1982.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://old.wdc.govt.nz/SearchCentre/Pages/CemeteryBurialDetails.aspx?CMID=3378&CMType=burial |title=Cemetery record details |publisher=Whangarei District Council |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref>
